bug_description.original: Heap-use-after-free in MuPDF's PDF object resolution path (seen in pdf_cache_object -> pdf_resolve_indirect -> pdf_resolve_indirect_chain). While resolving indirect objects the code accesses/writes memory that has already been freed, leading to heap corruption and crashes and potentially enabling further exploitation.
bug_description.normalized: The staged PDF page dictionary contains an `/Annots 23 0 R` entry, so page loading resolves annotation object 23 through `pdf_array_len` and `pdf_resolve_indirect_chain`. In the reproduced path object 23 is still represented by an unresolved `pdf_xref_entry` of type `'o'`, so `pdf_cache_object` saves a local alias `orig_x` to that entry and calls `pdf_load_obj_stm` to parse the containing object stream. During that helper, MuPDF re-fetches xref entries with the solidifying getter, which can reorganize the xref and free the old entry table. Control then returns to `pdf_cache_object`, which writes `orig_x->type = 'o'` in its `fz_always` block even though `orig_x` still points into the freed table, producing the saved 1-byte AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free write.

source.description: First project statement on the witnessed path that materializes vulnerability-relevant attacker data. The staged PDF page object shown by `strings` contains `/Annots 23 0 R`, and this lookup copies that crafted indirect annotations reference into `obj` for later resolution.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` contains `17 0 obj <</Annots 23 0 R ... /Type/Page>>`, so this statement reads the attacker-controlled `/Annots` entry from the parsed page dictionary and yields the indirect object later passed into `pdf_array_len`.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. After `pdf_load_obj_stm` has already triggered xref solidification and freed the old xref entry table, the `fz_always` block writes through the stale `orig_x` alias into freed heap memory.

root_cause.description: Root cause fixed by commit `608e9e9a4ec4d2013faf1b8f9ecec09e90f131f2`. Vulnerable code keeps `orig_x` as a raw alias to the current `pdf_xref_entry` across the `pdf_load_obj_stm` call even though that helper can solidify and relocate the xref; the patch re-fetches the entry after the helper instead of reusing this stale pointer.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker controls which indirect annotations object the page loader resolves. Here the `/Annots 23 0 R` value selected from the page dictionary drives the later object-stream resolution path that invalidates `orig_x`.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific admitted gate. The staged PDF page object includes `/Annots 23 0 R`, so after the document and page tree are accepted this branch is taken during page loading and the vulnerable annotations-resolution continuation is entered.

admitted_location.code: page->links = pdf_load_link_annots(ctx, doc, page, obj, number, page_ctm);

coarse_trace.summary: Page loading reads the crafted `/Annots 23 0 R` entry from the accepted PDF page object and passes it into annotation handling.
Resolving the indirect annotations array extracts object number 23 and routes through `pdf_resolve_indirect` into `pdf_cache_object`.
For an unresolved object-stream xref entry, `pdf_cache_object` saves `orig_x`, then `pdf_load_obj_stm` reparses the object stream and solidifies the xref, freeing the table that `orig_x` points into.
Control returns to the `fz_always` cleanup in `pdf_cache_object`, which writes through the stale `orig_x` alias and triggers the saved heap-use-after-free.

fine_trace.note: The staged page object contains `/Annots 23 0 R`, so this dictionary lookup materializes the attacker-controlled indirect annotations reference into `obj` for the rest of the vulnerable path.
The annotations value from step 1 is still an indirect object, so `RESOLVE(obj)` dispatches into `pdf_resolve_indirect_chain` to load the referenced object before treating it as an array.
Indirect resolution converts the attacker-selected annotations reference into concrete xref object number 23, the object that `pdf_cache_object` will now fetch.
The object number from step 3 is handed to `pdf_cache_object`, moving the vulnerable path from indirect-object resolution into xref-entry caching.

Caching loads the current xref entry pointer for object 23. On the crashing path this entry is an unresolved object-stream member (`x->type == 'o'`) with no cached object yet, so later code will try to populate it from the object stream.
Inside the `x->type == 'o'` arm, the entry is still unresolved, so this branch is taken and `pdf_cache_object` enters the object-stream loading path instead of returning a cached object.

Before calling the helper, vulnerable code saves a second local alias to the same xref entry. That alias is meant to survive until the `fz_always` cleanup, but no refresh happens if the helper reorganizes the xref.

The object-stream loader reparses the containing object stream for the target object. While doing so it re-fetches member xref entries with the solidifying getter, so this call may return a current `x` from a reorganized xref while leaving `orig_x` unchanged.

While parsing the object stream, the helper re-fetches the member xref entry for the current object number with `pdf_get_xref_entry_no_null`. The saved ASan free stack identifies this exact getter call as the source operation that enters the solidifying xref lookup path.

The getter from step 9 calls `pdf_get_xref_entry(..., solidify_if_needed=1)`, so `pdf_get_xref_entry_aux` reaches `ensure_solid_xref` and frees the old xref-entry table before returning a replacement entry pointer. Because `orig_x` from step 7 still points into that table, this free turns it into a dangling pointer.

Sink. After step 8 returns to the `fz_always` cleanup, vulnerable code writes through `orig_x` instead of re-fetching the entry from the current xref layout. Because step 10 already freed the backing table, this is the saved 1-byte heap-use-after-free write at `pdf_cache_object:2504`.

format.name: PDF
format.contract: The staged witness is a PDF whose page object contains `/Annots 23 0 R` and whose referenced annotations object is resolved through object-stream loading (`/Type/ObjStm`). Reaching the bug requires that resolving that specific indirect annotations object drives `pdf_cache_object` down the unresolved object-stream path where `pdf_load_obj_stm` solidifies the xref before `orig_x->type = 'o'` runs.
